thread:
sara_support: Hi team — ACME reported 502s from their private deployment. They say our endpoint api.redwood.internal 'can't be resolved' from their VPC after a recent infra change. They pasted dig/nslookup output below. Can someone check split-horizon / private hosted zone issues? :thinking_face:

alex_devops: Thanks. Can you paste the raw dig output + /etc/resolv.conf from one of their failing hosts? Also confirm VPC ID and zone name used for private hosted zone.

sara_support: Pasting what ACME sent (sensitive info redacted):

```
$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
search ip-10-0-0-0.ec2.internal
nameserver 172.31.0.2
options ndots:5
\n$ dig api.redwood.internal +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.redwood.internal +short
; global options: +cmd
; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
\n$ nslookup api.redwood.internal
Server: 172.31.0.2
Address: 172.31.0.2#53

*** Can't find api.redwood.internal: Name or service not known
```

They also tried curl and got: `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: api.redwood.internal`

anya_infra: Classic symptoms of a private hosted zone not being associated with the VPC that the query originates from (or a misconfigured resolver rule). Two quick checks: 1) confirm the private hosted zone ID (Z...); 2) confirm the VPC association list includes vpc-0a1b2c (their VPC). If the zone is created in a different account you also need a cross-account association.

mike_oncall: Also verify there's no custom DNS (DHCP options set) pointing to an on-prem forwarder that doesn't have the private zone. If their instances use a corporate forwarder that doesn't forward to Route53 Resolver, you'll see NXDOMAIN.

alex_devops: Can the customer run these to help narrow down?

```
dig @172.31.0.2 api.redwood.internal +trace
# and
dig +short @172.31.0.2 api.redwood.internal
# and
curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health
# and
sudo cat /etc/resolv.conf
```

sara_support: They ran the dig +trace and it shows the query stops at the VPC resolver without finding a zone — indicates the private hosted zone isn't associated or there's a conflicting public zone? They also mentioned this domain exists publicly for docs.redwood.com (different subdomain) — possible split-horizon name conflict.

anya_infra: Split-horizon note: If you have both a public hosted zone and a private hosted zone with the same name in different accounts/VPCs, resolution depends entirely on which VPC the query comes from and whether the private zone is associated. Things that commonly break this: 1) VPC wasn't associated after zone creation; 2) zone got disassociated during infra automation run; 3) Route53 Resolver rules that forward queries to another resolver that lacks the private zone.

netbot: FYI: Route53 private hosted zones require explicit VPC association. Also, Resolver rules are needed if queries are forwarded across accounts or into on-prem.

mike_oncall: Quick temporary workarounds while we investigate:
- Use curl --resolve to bypass DNS: `curl --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.2.4.5 https://api.redwood.internal/health` (replace with internal IP)
- Add an /etc/hosts entry on affected hosts (short-term)
- If k8s, add a CoreDNS stub domain mapping to the VPC resolver or create a configmap with hosts

alex_devops: Additional checks for them to run and share here so we can escalate if needed:
- `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "api.redwood.internal"` (or check console) and copy zone ID
- `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z/ID` to confirm VPCs associated
- If using cross-account private zones: list VPC associations for the consumer account and check `AssociateVPCWithHostedZone` ops
- Check Route53 Resolver rule associations: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0a1b2c`

sara_support: I asked ACME for zone ID and VPC ID. They returned: zone Z0XYZEXAMPLE, vpc-0a1b2c. They also show a recent terraform apply 2 days ago that touched route53_zone_association resources.

anya_infra: That smells like an automation regression. If terraform removed and re-added associations, it's possible the association ended up in the wrong account or with the wrong VPC. Please ask them to check the hosted zone associations in the AWS console (Route53 > Hosted zones > Private hosted zone details > Associated VPCs).

mike_oncall: If the zone is associated correctly but still NXDOMAIN, please confirm there are no DNS firewall rules or egress allowlist blocking outbound UDP/TCP 53 from the VPC or the resolver endpoints. Also check security groups on Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints if using those — they must allow 53.

alex_devops: If they confirm the zone is missing association, fix is: either associate the zone to the correct VPC (console or `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone`) or restore the terraform state that tracked the association. If it's a cross-account zone, follow the cross-account association flow (owner account creates the association authorization, consumer calls associate).

sara_support: ACME confirmed the private hosted zone was associated only with a tooling VPC (vpc-0999tool) not their prod VPC. They will request association and report back.

mike_oncall: Great. After they associate, ask them to run `dig @172.31.0.2 api.redwood.internal +short` from an affected host and also `dig +trace` to ensure resolution. If pods still cache negative responses, a node/kube-dns restart may be needed: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n kube-system` or restart the node's systemd-resolved cache.

sara_support: ACME did the association and the dig now returns the private IP. They restarted k8s coredns and curl succeeds. They thanked us and will follow up if anything else. :tada:

mike_oncall: Closing notes for runbook update: add a checklist for private DNS failures — 1) check VPC association, 2) verify Resolver rules/forwarders, 3) confirm DHCP options/custom DNS, 4) confirm security groups/egress allowlist, 5) clear DNS caches. I'll add this to the support runbook. @anya_infra can you add a short troubleshooting snippet to infra docs? :+1:

anya_infra: Yep will add a short doc with commands and the common terraform pitfall.

netbot: Incident closed (manual).
